builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: On the Sparsity of Direct Preference Optimization: Weight Disentanglement in the NTK Regime
summary: This work provides a theoretical and empirical explanation for why DPO produces sparse parameter updates, rather than replacing an existing training method with a new one. The cost is limited: understanding the NTK-based analysis and the dual-sparsity claim adds conceptual complexity but no direct infrastructure requirement beyond what DPO already demands. The main risk is that the findings remain a mechanistic explanation tied to specific models and datasets, and the 35x interference reduction is demonstrated on GPT-2, so it may not transfer reliably to larger production models or different alignment tasks.
rationale: The paper is primarily an explanatory analysis of DPO rather than a deployable technique, making it relevant for understanding but not immediate adoption under constrained infrastructure.
technique: Dual sparsity analysis of DPO for weight disentanglement
